text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 2.8% today as oil prices climbed on escalating U.S.-Iran military tensions in the Middle East. U.S. crude hit $90 a barrel on September 1st following American strikes against Iran, and continued gains Wednesday as tit-for-tat strikes kept the region unstable—a genuine supply risk that pushes up the price of oil globally. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly improve profitability on the barrels they pump.

The two-week rally of nearly 5% fits a clear pattern: oil was trading around $80 in late August, then jumped to $83–90 as geopolitical risk spiked. This is a straightforward supply-and-demand story—when investors worry Middle East production could be disrupted, they bid up oil futures, and integrated oil companies like ConocoPhillips benefit from the price appreciation.
